content:
If I formalize a short proof from a book (~20 lines of code, but nontrivial), should I include it in docs/references.bib?
It seems fitting, but OTOH I'm not going to mention the book in the module docstring because it's not significant enough. So the reference will have no docstring pointing at it.

Oh if you're not going to mention the book explicitly then there's little point putting it in the references: people will see the reference and think "ooh where is that used" and then search mathlib and find nothing and will just be confused.
It would be good to mention it in the PR at least, so there's some record of it.

Snir Broshi said:

If you're talking about Sierpinski's book in your ordinal commutation PRs then I think that should earn a mention in the module docstring.
Oh right, now that we moved it to a new file that makes more sense
